title: Identity and pasting equations for exchange
statement:
Use the inverse images $u^{-1}$ on the bounded below derived categories of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], the derived direct images $Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] with the adjunctions $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], the composition and identity isomorphisms $c^D_{u,v}:v^{-1}u^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(u\circ v)^{-1}$, $e^D_X:\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ of the inverse images [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], and the composition isomorphisms $d^D_{u,v}:R(u\circ v)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_*\circ Rv_*$ of the derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition]. For a cartesian square $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $g':X'\to X$, let $\Ex_\square:g^{-1}Rf_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}$ be the derived exchange transformation [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]. Outer rectangles of pasted cartesian squares are cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. Then, as natural transformations of functors between bounded below derived categories:

1. (Identity square.) For $f:X\to Y$ and the square $\square_f=(f,f,\mathrm{id}_Y,\mathrm{id}_X)$,
$$
 Rf_*(e^D_X)\circ\Ex_{\square_f}=e^D_{Y}Rf_*:\ \mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}Rf_*\longrightarrow Rf_*,
$$
i.e. $\Ex_{\square_f}$ is the identity of $Rf_*$ once $\mathrm{id}^{-1}$ is identified with the identity functor by $e^D$.
2. (Horizontal pasting, composing the base changes.) For $\square_1=(f,f',g,g')$ and a cartesian square $\square_2=(f',f'',h,h')$ with $h:Y''\to Y'$, $h':X''\to X'$, $f'':X''\to Y''$, the outer rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1=(f,f'',g\circ h,g'\circ h')$ satisfies
$$
 \Ex_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}=(Rf''_*c^D_{g',h'})\circ(\Ex_{\square_2}g'^{-1})\circ(h^{-1}\Ex_{\square_1})\circ((c^D_{g,h})^{-1}Rf_*):
$$
$$
 (gh)^{-1}Rf_*\to h^{-1}g^{-1}Rf_*\to h^{-1}Rf'_*g'^{-1}\to Rf''_*h'^{-1}g'^{-1}\to Rf''_*(g'h')^{-1}.
$$
3. (Vertical pasting, composing the direct images.) For $\square_1$ as above and a cartesian square $\square_3=(e,e',g',g'')$ with $e:W\to X$, $e':W'\to X'$, $g'':W'\to W$, the outer rectangle $\square_1\circ\square_3=(f\circ e,f'\circ e',g,g'')$ satisfies
$$
 \Ex_{\square_1\circ\square_3}=((d^D_{f',e'})^{-1}g''^{-1})\circ(Rf'_*\Ex_{\square_3})\circ(\Ex_{\square_1}Re_*)\circ(g^{-1}d^D_{f,e}):
$$
$$
 g^{-1}R(fe)_*\to g^{-1}Rf_*Re_*\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}Re_*\to Rf'_*Re'_*g''^{-1}\to R(f'e')_*g''^{-1}.
$$

proof.text: *The exchange transformation as a mate.* For a cartesian square $\square=(f,f',g,g')$ put $\mathcal A=\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$, $\mathcal B=\Dplus(X_{\Et})$, $\mathcal C=\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$, $\mathcal D=\Dplus(X'_{\Et})$, $L_1=f^{-1}\dashv R_1=Rf_*$ and $L_2=f'^{-1}\dashv R_2=Rf'_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction], $G=g^{-1}$, $H=g'^{-1}$. Then $\theta^D_\square:L_2G\to HL_1$ is a square in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and, by [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], $\Ex_\square=(\theta^D_\square)^\flat:GR_1\to R_2H$ is its mate. Only the equality $fg'=gf'$ of each square enters, through $\theta^D_\square$. All identities below are identities of mates, computed in this dictionary.

proof.text: *Identity square.* By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting] (1), $\theta^D_{\square_f}=((e^D_X)^{-1}f^{-1})\circ(f^{-1}e^D_Y)$. Read with $L_1=L_2=f^{-1}$ (one adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ on both rows), this is the square $\iota=\mathrm{id}_{f^{-1}}:L_2\,\mathrm{id}\to\mathrm{id}\,L_1$ (with $G=H=\mathrm{id}$) whiskered by $\sigma=e^D_Y:\mathrm{id}_Y^{-1}\to\mathrm{id}$ on the side of $G$ and by $\tau=(e^D_X)^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to\mathrm{id}_X^{-1}$ on the side of $H$, i.e. $\theta^D_{\square_f}=(\tau L_1)\circ\iota\circ(L_2\sigma)$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker], $\Ex_{\square_f}=(Rf_*\tau)\circ\iota^\flat\circ(\sigma Rf_*)$. The mate $\iota^\flat$ of $\mathrm{id}_{f^{-1}}$ for $G=H=\mathrm{id}$ is its conjugate, which is $\mathrm{id}_{Rf_*}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (4) (equivalently [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]). Hence $\Ex_{\square_f}=Rf_*((e^D_X)^{-1})\circ e^D_YRf_*$, and composing with $Rf_*(e^D_X)$ gives (1).

proof.text:
*Horizontal pasting.* The rectangle $\square_2\cdot\square_1$ is cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting] (2), and since $c^D_{g,h}$ is invertible,
$$
 \theta^D_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}=(c^D_{g',h'}f^{-1})\circ P\circ(f''^{-1}(c^D_{g,h})^{-1}),\qquad P=(h'^{-1}\theta^D_{\square_1})\circ(\theta^D_{\square_2}g^{-1}):f''^{-1}h^{-1}g^{-1}\to h'^{-1}g'^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$
$P$ is the pasting along $G,H$ of the squares $\alpha=\theta^D_{\square_1}$ ($G=g^{-1}$, $H=g'^{-1}$, $L_1=f^{-1}$, $L_2=f'^{-1}$) and $\beta=\theta^D_{\square_2}$ ($G_2=h^{-1}$, $H_2=h'^{-1}$, $L_3=f''^{-1}$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (1) its mate (adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ and $f''^{-1}\dashv Rf''_*$) is $P^\flat=(\Ex_{\square_2}g'^{-1})\circ(h^{-1}\Ex_{\square_1})$ (step 1). The square $\theta^D_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}$ is $P$ whiskered by $\sigma=(c^D_{g,h})^{-1}:(gh)^{-1}\to h^{-1}g^{-1}$ on the side of $G$ and by $\tau=c^D_{g',h'}:h'^{-1}g'^{-1}\to(g'h')^{-1}$ on the side of $H$; by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker] its mate, which is $\Ex_{\square_2\cdot\square_1}$ (step 1, [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]), equals $(Rf''_*c^D_{g',h'})\circ P^\flat\circ((c^D_{g,h})^{-1}Rf_*)$. This is (2).

proof.text:
*Vertical pasting.* The rectangle $\square_1\circ\square_3$ is cartesian [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting] (3),
$$
 \theta^D_{\square_1\circ\square_3}=(g''^{-1}c^D_{f,e})\circ Q\circ((c^D_{f',e'})^{-1}g^{-1}),\qquad Q=(\theta^D_{\square_3}f^{-1})\circ(e'^{-1}\theta^D_{\square_1}):e'^{-1}f'^{-1}g^{-1}\to g''^{-1}e^{-1}f^{-1}.
$$
$Q$ is the pasting along the adjunctions of $\alpha=\theta^D_{\square_1}$ ($L_1=f^{-1}$, $L_2=f'^{-1}$, $G=g^{-1}$, $H=g'^{-1}$) and $\beta=\theta^D_{\square_3}$ ($L_3=e^{-1}$, $L_4=e'^{-1}$, $K=g''^{-1}$), a square for the composite adjunctions $e^{-1}f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*Re_*$ and $e'^{-1}f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*Re'_*$; by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (2) and step 1 its mate is $Q^\flat=(Rf'_*\Ex_{\square_3})\circ(\Ex_{\square_1}Re_*):g^{-1}Rf_*Re_*\to Rf'_*Re'_*g''^{-1}$. Now change the adjunctions: on the top row replace $e^{-1}f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*Re_*$ by $(fe)^{-1}\dashv R(fe)_*$ through $\sigma=c^D_{f,e}:e^{-1}f^{-1}\to(fe)^{-1}$, whose conjugate is $d^D_{f,e}:R(fe)_*\to Rf_*Re_*$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition]; by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (3)(b) the square $(g''^{-1}\sigma)\circ Q$ has mate $Q^\flat\circ(g^{-1}d^D_{f,e})$. On the bottom row replace $e'^{-1}f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*Re'_*$ by $(f'e')^{-1}\dashv R(f'e')_*$ through $\tau=(c^D_{f',e'})^{-1}:(f'e')^{-1}\to e'^{-1}f'^{-1}$, whose conjugate is $(d^D_{f',e'})^{-1}$ (the conjugate of the inverse of an isomorphism is the inverse of its conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]); by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] (3)(a) the square $(g''^{-1}\sigma)\circ Q\circ(\tau g^{-1})=\theta^D_{\square_1\circ\square_3}$ has mate $((d^D_{f',e'})^{-1}g''^{-1})\circ Q^\flat\circ(g^{-1}d^D_{f,e})$. By step 1 this mate is $\Ex_{\square_1\circ\square_3}$, which is (3).

split_report.summary: Statement made precise: the identity law with the identity isomorphisms e^D of the derived inverse images, horizontal pasting (Stacks 0E47, composing the base changes, with c^D) and vertical pasting (Stacks 0E46, composing the direct images, with c^D and the derived direct-image composition isomorphisms d^D, defined as conjugates of c^D as in Stacks 0D6E); stmt_deps rewritten. The imported one-paragraph proof is replaced by four steps from the mate calculus: the dictionary Ex = mate of theta^D (definition), and for each law the corresponding pasting law of theta^D (new node lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting) transported by the Mathlib mate lemmas (new leaf lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting: mateEquiv_vcomp, mateEquiv_hcomp, mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_vcomp, conjugateEquiv_mateEquiv_vcomp, conjugateEquiv_id) and the whiskering lemma (new node lem-weil-pbc-mate-whisker, not in Mathlib). The citation of lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-replacement is dropped: with Ex defined as the mate it is a pointer (it concerns the computation on resolutions, not used here). New: lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition (c^D, e^D and coherence; lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition has no associativity clause), def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate (leaf). lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-coherence (same unit, imported) states the same pasting laws plus resolution independence: merge candidate.
